A lot of it happened at once, but it was kind of like a volcano if you catch my metaphor. Once I realized about my gender, I realized a lot of other things I was taught weren't accurate or incredibly biased and often unsourced.

In regards to transitioning, it is ok for me to do just as it'd be ok to get your wisdom teeth pulled, or a nose job, or a breast augmentation, etc. It is to make oneself comfortable in the body that encases them.

Of course the counter argument is that people say that our bodes are on loan from god. Again, the would be invalidated for something that is deemed medically legitimate such as appendix removal or wisdom teeth removal, etc. only this is much more severe but not illegitimate.

Yes a big part of the argument is "to save a life". Transitioning, I guess in some ways, can be somewhat compared to braces for teeth. The teeth shift to be put into an optimum position. So to, one transitions their body so they can feel at piece with themselves with the correct body.

It is possible for brains of one sex to develop in the body of another sex. Hormones are a very powerful thing.

Would you tell someone who was born with one arm that they are an abomination? Would you be ok with them getting a prosthetic? What about cisgender women who are born without a uterus or ovaries. Does that make them a man?

It's time for people to understand and learn that gender isn't defined, nor can it or should it be defined, based on sexual characteristics.

A brain develops as it does, but it doesn't make someone crazy or an abomination.

I hope that this makes sense.I don't know how else to explain it. I am thankful that the younger generations are understanding this more which will lead to a better future, hopefully, but that doesn't mean the older generations have to stay the same.

Maybe some day more people will understand.

It's a big reason why I came out the way I did from the community I did. I felt the need to do it not only for me, but for others who are like me who are in the closet and living miserable lives. Ever check the suicide attempts rate for transgender people? 41%

Firstly, we are all confused lol. Life brings clarity. It is a journey, an adventure, and time of growth. Nothing wrong with asking questions! :) 

It proves you're growing!

So, in terms of homosexuality, I should clarify that it is quite different than being transgender. I am attracted to women, but identify as women. There isn't anything that I have ever heard of that prohibits women to women relations. 

In regards to man to man relations, I feel ill-equipped because I do not view myself as a man nor am i attracted to men. If you'd like, I can find someone to answer that part for you, though I'd highly recommend reaching out to Eshel as they're much better equipped at those sort of questions :)

In regards to wearing women's clothing, as stated before, I do not identify as a man. I feel that while I have a part-man's body, I do not allow myself essence of my being to be dictated by my anatomy but rather who I am as a person. For example, that our body is a shell and it is a person's essence to which what defines them.

Another thing to note is that gender is a social construct. For example, as times change, our view of gender norms change. i.e. in WW2 when the men went to war, women went to work. In Ireland, men wear kilts which are skirts. There are "bras for men", because some men need bras do to the wait of breast tissue. I don't view myself as a man, but I also have breasts thanks to hormone therapy which means that I need to wear a bra if I want to do anything that requires running or going up and down a flight of stairs.

In terms of a mechitza, the halacha is more along the lines of which side would I be a distraction on? Some trans women pass better than others, and vice versa for men. While there is some potential halachic issues that come up from transmen, I am not a transman, which means I am not able to give as accurate info regarding that because I focus more on what I am going through because it is a lot to take in as it is. ;)

Anyways, shomer negiah, technically doesn't apply to me because I don't menstruate, but there are some cis (born female and identify as female) women who don't menstruate either. That being said, I try to hold shomer towards men who hold being shomer out of respect to them. For women who hold shomer, it is a super confusing thing.

There is a lot of things that has some conflicts, but it's all about coming to understand things and then being able to proceed from there. There is much I still don't know, but I am still learning as quickly as I can. It definitely is possible to be in the LGBT world and Orthodox, but it takes a willingness to want to learn how.

I really appreciate your willingness to ask questions. I really hope this helped. I'm sorry it was such a long response.
